issues.detail: Error handling is limited to a brief mention of 401/402 codes; there is no guidance on rate limits (429), retries, text length limits, empty or invalid voice IDs, or failed voice-clone uploads.
The two examples only point back to earlier steps with a one-line description and no full input/output demonstration, and none covers voice cloning or the Node.js SDK end to end.

scenarios.name: stream-ulaw-for-phone-bot
scenarios.rationale: B uses `client.text_to_speech.stream`, iterates the chunks, sets `ulaw_8000` and `eleven_flash_v2_5`, and reads `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` from the environment, so it meets every rubric item. A gets the model, format and env var right but uses the raw WebSocket stream-input endpoint instead of the SDK `text_to_speech.stream` method, so it misses the main rubric item.

scenarios.name: clone-voice-and-narrate-mp3
scenarios.rationale: Both use ivc.create, eleven_multilingual_v2, previous_text/next_text, iterate bytes to mp3, and mention consent; B adds sentence-level fallback chunking, the reuse note, and an older-SDK note, while A passes paths directly (possibly invalid) but openly flags that uncertainty.

scenarios.name: node-tts-migration-and-voice-lookup
scenarios.rationale: Both swap to @elevenlabs/elevenlabs-js, import ElevenLabsClient, call textToSpeech.convert with modelId eleven_flash_v2_5 and outputFormat, and use ELEVENLABS_API_KEY; A explicitly looks up the voice with voices.search and says to do so instead of hard-coding IDs, while B pushes an env-var voice ID first and uses voices.search only as a fallback with pageSize 1, which is weaker on the 'advise using voices.search' point.
